Subject: StellarSync - Technical runbook & next steps (integration questions)

Hi Olivia — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a handful of follow-ups so we can scope a short pilot/POC: 

Recap (agreed on call)
- Goal: embed Redwood inference for realtime recommendations and a light reranking step on search results.
- Expected QPS: ~100–150 peak search requests, avg 60 rps. Typical context lengths ~ 300–800 tokens (summary + metadata).
- Requirements: PII minimization, region constraint (US), SLA for 99.9% availability during business hours.

Open technical questions we promised to confirm:
1) SDK & Auth: do you prefer API keys or mTLS/SSO on day-1? Any procurement constraints for credential rotation?
2) Routing & regions: we should pin to us-west for latency; any multi-region failover needs?
3) Structured output & tool-calling: do you need the model to emit structured JSON for the reranker inputs, or will Redwood post-process free-form text?
4) Embeddings & reranker: will embeddings be generated at ingest time (offline) or at query time? Do you plan to use our embeddings service or host locally?
5) Schema + token limits: sample request/response size estimates so we can advise on model variant and max_tokens. Any hard stop sequences we must honor?
6) Streaming: do you need token-by-token streaming to the client, or is batch response OK?

Attachments: I attached the integration checklist and a strawman schema we sketched during the call.

Suggested next steps
- Tessa to run a short tech write-up with recommended SDK code paths and config (auth, routing, batching).
- Olivia / Samir to confirm embeddings strategy (ingest vs query) and give a sample payload (one item).
- Schedule 45m follow-up next week to finalize pilot success metrics.

If you can reply inline to the six questions above that will let us produce a targeted runbook. Thanks — CCing Tessa and Markus for technical alignment.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: StellarSync - Technical runbook & next steps (integration questions)

Thanks Camila — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers inline below.

1) SDK & Auth: procurement prefers API keys to start; we can add mTLS later for the dedicated/private option. Keys must rotate every 90 days; can you confirm automated rotation support?

2) Routing & regions: primary is us-west; we'd like automatic failover to us-east only if latency exceeds 200ms or instance health fails.

3) Structured output & tool-calling: we'd prefer the model to emit structured JSON for the reranker input to avoid brittle parsing. Example: {"candidates": [{"id": string, "score": float, "features": {...}}]}

4) Embeddings & reranker: plan is hybrid — generate embeddings at ingest for historical data (offline) and query-time for user prompts. We'll use Redwood's embeddings endpoint initially.

5) Schema + token limits: typical response size after reranking ~ 250 tokens. Max user prompt with context ~ 1200 tokens. Prefer hard stop sequences when returning JSON (we can use "\n\nEND_JSON" as a delimiter if needed).

6) Streaming: streaming preferred for UI feel on longer responses, but not strictly required for short rerank replies. If streaming is enabled, we only need deltas for the final JSON object (i.e., stream until the full JSON is complete).

I've attached a representative payload (stellarsync-example-schema.json) and can share more after background export. Samir and I are available Wed/Thu afternoon PST for the 45m follow-up.

Thanks,
Olivia Grant

Hi all — quick technical notes based on Olivia's responses. I kept this tight so you can paste into your runbook.

Auth / SDK
- Day-1: API keys with 90-day rotation. Redwood supports key revocation and short-lived keys via our control plane; we can automate rotation using our API or Vault/HCS connectors.
- SDK path: use the official Redwood SDK for JS/Python. Example (pseudo):
  - Initialize client with api_key env var.
  - Use client.request({model: 'redwood-rt-large', mode: 'chat', stream: false, max_tokens: 512})

Routing & region failover
- Pin to us-west region. Configure a policy: prefer us-west; failover to us-east when median p95 latency > 200ms or health-check fails for >30s. We can provide a managed policy JSON for your infra.

Embeddings & reranker
- Hybrid flow works well: offline embeddings for corpus + query-time embeddings for freshness. Match embedding model across both paths for vector drift control.
- For reranker, prefer the model to emit structured JSON (tool-calling / structured output). That reduces parsing errors and latency for downstream scoring.

Request/Response schema (chat vs completions)
- Recommendation: use chat API for multi-turn behaviors (context windows, system messages, turn metadata). Use completions for single-shot scoring if you want simpler token accounting.
- Tokenization & max_tokens: with 1200 token prompt + expected 250 token output, provision for ~1500 total tokens. For safety, set model max_tokens to 1600. Note some quantized variants have lower sequence limits; we'll propose compatible variants.
- Stop sequences: since you need strict JSON, configure both a hard stop token (e.g., "END_JSON") and content-filtering hooks. If streaming, buffer until the stop token is observed before emitting final JSON to the client.
- Streaming semantics: our streaming emits chunk deltas (partial tokens). For JSON outputs we recommend either: 1) stream raw tokens with a final flush on detection of END_JSON, or 2) return a short "ack" stream and then send the full JSON once complete (less error-prone for parsers).

Performance knobs
- Batching & caching: enable prefix KV caching for repeated context to cut token costs. For your throughput, batching windows of 20–50ms should improve utilization without adding visible latency.
- Reranker approach: 2-step — coarse candidate generation (fast model), then fine rerank with structured-scoring model. We'll size GPU/throughput for p95 latency targets once you confirm concurrency.

I'll draft these as bullets in the runbook and include recommended model variants and a short example SDK config. Let me know if you want sample code for streaming JSON-safe parsing.

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
tessa@redwood.com
